defects: Hypothesis uses `BoundedVariationOn f s` (global bounded variation) instead of `LocallyBoundedVariationOn f s`, a strictly stronger assumption than the informal statement ("locally bounded variation") and gold require.

Uses `Monotone p`, `Monotone n` (monotonicity required over the entire type α) instead of `MonotoneOn p s`, `MonotoneOn q s` (monotonicity only on s), imposing an unwarranted stronger requirement not supported by the informal statement or provable from mere local bounded variation on s.
Equality is only required pointwise on s (`∀ x ∈ s, f x = p x - n x`) rather than the global function equality `f = p - q` from gold, changing what is actually being asserted about p, n outside s.

The 'combined increments equal the total variation' clause is weakened to a single aggregate equation `eVariationOn p s + eVariationOn n s = eVariationOn f s` instead of gold's pointwise-for-every-pair condition `∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, (p y - p x) + (q y - q x) = variationOnFromTo f s x y`, losing the stronger subinterval-additivity content.

Uses `eVariationOn` (ℝ≥0∞-valued, unsigned total variation) instead of `variationOnFromTo` (ℝ-valued signed variation between two points), a different mathematical object than gold's, not just a notational variant.
